article.title: Iran says agreement with Oman would not mean the reopening of Hormuz
article.summary: Iran says agreement with Oman would not mean the reopening of HormuzIranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned on Sunday that Iran's anticipated agreement with Oman to govern the Strait of Hormuz will not trigger a reopening of the waterway.In comments to Al-Araby Al-Jadeed, Araghchi said Iran will provide details of the agreement and the new route maps to countries participating in a meeting with Gulf states in the Omani capital tomorrow, adding that the agreement does not “in any way” signal that the strait will reopen, which is conditional on the US honouring its commitments under the Memorandum of Understanding signed in Islamabad, he said.“Iran believes that the responsibility for ensuring security and stability in the region lies solely with the countries of the region,” Araghchi added.

article.title: Iran authorities say 1 killed, 3 injured as merchant vessel struck in Hormuz
article.summary: A ship was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, killing one person and injuring three, local Iranian authorities said, as Tehran and Washington clash over the strategic waterway.“A merchant vessel was struck around 5am this morning off the coasts of Hengam and Qeshm islands. One person was killed and three others were injured,” Qeshm city governor Amir Teymouri said, according to state TV, without specifying the origin of the strike.Several explosions were reported overnight around Qeshm, the largest island in the Hormuz strait.The deadly incident comes a day before ameetingbetween Iran and Gulf states in Oman, which also borders the strait, over the blockaded route crucial for global oil and gas trade.Control over the strait has become a major flashpoint in the conflict between Iran and the United States in theirsix-month war.In retaliation for attacks by the United States and Israel that started the war on February 28, Iran has blocked the waterway, a passage that was previou...

article.title: Iran-Oman understanding does not provide for immediate reopening of Strait of Hormuz, Tasnim reports
article.summary: Sept 12 (Reuters) - An understanding between Iran and Oman does not provide for the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz but establishes the basis on which it could reopen, an Iranian source told the semi-official Tasnim news agency on Saturday.The source said the arrangement would be a step towards Iran exercising sovereignty over the strait and that its reopening depended entirely on the United States meeting Tehran's conditions.(Reporting by Dubai newsroom, Editing by Louise Heavens)

article.title: No signed Hormuz deal expected yet from Oman meeting on Monday, Iranian official says
article.summary: Sept 12 (Reuters) - A meeting between Iran and Gulf states planned for Monday in Oman will be a chance to discuss issues including the Strait of Hormuz, but is not expected to yield a signed agreement over the blockaded waterway, a senior Iranian official said on Saturday.Iran has been negotiating for months with Oman, which controls the opposite bank of the strait, over a deal that would govern transport through it. Oman has long said its negotiations are supported by other Arab countries in the Gulf.
